domain.title: Positive Classroom Environment
domain.description: Missouri Standard 5 defines the job as building a place where learning happens — environment, engagement, interaction, self-motivation. Not compliance. Not control. Three views of one room: person · structure · relationship.

claims.statement: The teacher uses an understanding of individual/group motivation and behavior to create a learning environment that encourages active engagement in learning, positive social interaction, and self-motivation.

sources.title: Missouri Teacher Standards — Standard 5: Positive Classroom Environment

bands.label: K–2
bands.driver: Regulation is external and taught — routines and structure are supplied by the teacher and rehearsed like content.

strands.5.1: Engagement shows in the body — leaning in, blurting about the content, hands on materials. Movement and talk are signs of thinking. Teacher supplies regulation; frequent specific praise.
strands.5.2: Short work cycles; transitions modeled and rehearsed (songs, signals, practiced routes); heavy visual structure.
strands.5.3: Belonging built through naming, greeting, and daily ritual; repair in simple, concrete language.

bands.driver: Self-regulation emerging, peers rising — teacher shifts from directing to prompting as students begin to manage themselves.

strands.5.1: Engagement looks more internal — sustained attention, on-topic peer talk, extending questions, persistence, connecting to earlier learning.
strands.5.2: Longer work cycles; students manage their own materials and movement within a set structure.
strands.5.3: Students take on classroom roles and simple restorative conversations; norms made explicit and revisited.

bands.driver: Identity, autonomy, peers primary — correction must protect adolescent face; students help set norms and run the room.

strands.5.1: Engagement runs on relevance and voice; cognitive investment over compliance; students help set re-engagement norms.
strands.5.2: Students move between formats (discussion → group → independent) with minimal cueing; teacher designs, students run it.
strands.5.3: Students co-own norms and lead repair; identity and peer-belonging are central; culture becomes partly student-run.

strands.title: Behavior & Engagement
strands.subtitle: The people, in the moment.
strands.description: Keep students engaged and the class in motion; handle misbehavior with least disruption.

continuum.text: Recognizes principles of classroom management, motivation and engagement.
Knows how classroom management, motivation, and engagement relate to one another and has knowledge of strategies and techniques for using this to promote student interest and learning.
Demonstrates basic classroom management techniques and addresses misbehavior to avoid the disruption of instruction.
Uses effective classroom management techniques including addressing misbehavior promptly and effectively with the least disruption of instruction.
Adapts and develops classroom management techniques that address all student misbehavior ensuring little or no disruption of instruction.
Shares with others effective classroom management techniques that reduce the likelihood of misbehavior ensuring little or no disruptions to instruction.

strands.title: Culture & Belonging
strands.subtitle: The relational field.
strands.description: Build a culture where students belong, trust each other, and want to learn.

continuum.text: Recognizes the influence of classroom, school, and community culture on student relationships and the impact on the classroom environment and learning.
Recognizes and identifies the influence of classroom, school and community culture on student relationships and the impact on the classroom environment and learning.
Builds awareness of the culture of the school and community in order to influence student relationships and build an effective classroom learning environment.
Develops a positive culture in the classroom and school to positively affect student relationships and learning.
Maintains and enhances a positive culture in the classroom and school, creating a classroom environment which promotes positive student relationships and learning.
Actively engages students in discussing and evaluating the culture of the classroom, school and community to positively impact relationships and learning.

not_yet_connected.statement: Durable learning reveals itself over time, through what persists; it is built by repeated, spaced practice.

sources.title: The Science of Learning (2nd ed.)
sources.excerpt: Completion of assignments and absence of errors does not necessarily equate to long-lasting learning. There are many strategies which support short-term performance that inflate the appearance of learning without deepening meaningful, longer-lasting learning.
